promptText: When an owner wants a collection or soft-brand option for a hotel conversion in Mexico, which brands are commonly considered?
rawResponse:
Here’s a structured overview of the **most commonly considered soft‑brand or “collection” options** when an owner in Mexico seeks to convert an existing property (often an independent hotel) into a branded offering. These brands allow for flexibility—preserving existing character while benefiting from a recognized platform and distribution.

---

##  Key Soft‑Brand Options Commonly Used in Mexico

### 1. **Marriott International**
- **Autograph Collection**: A lifestyle/upscale soft‑brand geared toward boutique or unique hotels, offering independence paired with Marriott’s loyalty and distribution. It’s growing quickly in Mexico, particularly among all‑inclusive resorts in Cancún. ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))
- **Tribute Portfolio**: Focuses on design-forward, warm, and curated experiences. Aimed at both business and leisure travelers. Comparable to Hilton’s Curio Collection. ([hoteltechreport.com](https://hoteltechreport.com/news/hotel-brand-guide?utm_source=openai))
- **The Luxury Collection**: One of the earliest—launched in 1992—this high‑end soft brand is often used for converting historic or iconic buildings. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriott_International?utm_source=openai))

### 2. **Hilton**
- **Curio Collection by Hilton**: Positioned upscale-luxury; commonly used to convert independent or boutique hotels. Several conversions in Mexico’s Riviera Maya and cities like Monterrey and Tulum are recent examples. ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))
- **Tapestry Collection by Hilton**: A broader boutique soft brand within Hilton's portfolio. Offers more flexibility; examples include deals in Playa del Carmen. ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))
- **LXR Hotels & Resorts**: A luxury-focused soft brand under Hilton. ([whiteskyhospitality.com](https://whiteskyhospitality.com/hotel-brand-extensions-growth-strategy-or-dilution-trap/?utm_source=openai))
- **Spark by Hilton**: A newer mid-tier conversion brand introduced in 2025 in Mexico, designed specifically for converting existing properties, particularly in mid-size or emerging cities. ([thegatewithbriancohen.com](https://thegatewithbriancohen.com/what-is-a-conversion-brand-and-why-you-might-want-to-avoid-it/?utm_source=openai))

### 3. **IHG (InterContinental Hotels Group)**
- **Vignette Collection**: A flexible upscale to upper-upscale soft brand suited for conversions. ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))
- **Garner by IHG**: A midscale conversion brand launched in 2023, with rapid adoption across the region. One recent launch includes Garner Mazatlán Beach in Mexico. ([thegatewithbriancohen.com](https://thegatewithbriancohen.com/what-is-a-conversion-brand-and-why-you-might-want-to-avoid-it/?utm_source=openai))

### 4. **Wyndham Hotels & Resorts**
- **Trademark Collection by Wyndham**: A well-established boutique soft brand, widely used in Mexico—including deals with Grupo MX Hotels incorporating over 15 properties into the collection. ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))
- **Registry Collection**: A luxury-tier alternative within Wyndham’s soft-brand portfolio. ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))

### 5. **Choice Hotels**
- **Ascend Hotel Collection**: A soft-brand from Choice Hotels, targeting historic/upscale hotels. Competes with Wyndham’s Trademark and IHG’s voco, and is often used in lifestyle conversions. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascend_Collection?utm_source=openai))

### 6. **Other Soft-Brand Options**
- **Preferred Hotels & Resorts**: An independent soft-brand platform (not tied to major chains), often used for luxury or boutique properties. ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))
- **Oyo**, **Dot Hotels**: Emerging models—Oyo (India-based) targets mid-to-economy independents; Dot Hotels (Argentina-based) covers various segments. ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))
- **Gamma by Posadas**: A Mexican soft-brand for leisure or lifestyle conversions, operated by Grupo Posadas. ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))

---

##  Recent Examples & Regional Context in Mexico

- **Riviera Maya (Cancún, Playa del Carmen, Tulum)**: Numerous all‑inclusive resorts have converted to soft brands. Examples include:
  - **Marriott’s Autograph Collection** converting five all-inclusive resorts in Cancún.
  - **Hilton’s Curio Collection** openings in Monterrey and Tulum.
  - **Posadas’ Curamoria Collection** in Querétaro, San Miguel de Allende, and Tulum. ([costar.com](https://www.costar.com/article/1218949022/mexico-weathers-another-tourism-storm-faces-headwinds-in-2021?utm_source=openai))

- **IHG Growth Strategy**: In mid‑2026, IHG’s regional development VP highlighted that Mexico will represent about 50% of the company's future expansion in Latin America, underscoring how impactful soft brands are in the region. ([costar.com](https://www.costar.com/article/1775490468/soft-brands-conversions-drive-ihg-hotels-resorts-growth-in-caribbean-latin-america?edition=us&utm_source=openai))

---

##  Summary Table of Common Soft-Brand Choices in Mexico

Soft-Brand / Collection | Parent Chain | Positioning / Notes
--- | --- | ---
Autograph Collection | Marriott | Upscale lifestyle; historic/all-inclusive conversions
Tribute Portfolio | Marriott | Design-forward boutique
The Luxury Collection | Marriott | High-end, iconic/historic conversions
Curio Collection | Hilton | Upscale/luxury boutique
Tapestry Collection | Hilton | Lifestyle boutique
LXR Hotels & Resorts | Hilton | Luxury soft brand
Spark by Hilton | Hilton | Midscale conversion brand (Mexico launch 2025)
Vignette Collection | IHG | Upscale lifestyle conversions
Garner by IHG | IHG | Midscale conversion brand (Mexico examples)
Trademark Collection | Wyndham | Boutique soft brand; widely used in Mexico
Registry Collection | Wyndham | Luxury soft brand
Ascend Collection | Choice Hotels | Historic/upscale boutique conversions
Preferred Hotels & Resorts | Independent | Luxury/boutique independent affiliator
Oyo / Dot Hotels | Oyo, Dot Hotels | Mid-to-economy indie conversions
Gamma | Posadas | Mexican lifestyle/leisure soft brand

---

##  Recommendations for Owners in Mexico

- **For boutique or lifestyle hotels** aiming to retain character: consider **Marriott’s Autograph or Tribute**, **Hilton’s Curio or Tapestry**, **Wyndham’s Trademark**, or **Choice’s Ascend**.
- **For luxury or historic conversions**: **The Luxury Collection**, **LXR by Hilton**, or **Preferred Hotels & Resorts** offer high-end soft-branding.
- **For cost-sensitive or midscale projects**: **Spark by Hilton** or **Garner by IHG** are designed precisely for conversions with lighter investment.
- **For owners seeking domestic affiliation**: **Gamma (Posadas)** is a strong Mexican option with regional market reach.
- **For lean, independent affiliation**: platforms like **Oyo** or **Dot Hotels** may be considerations—especially for economy-to-midscale properties.
